title: Why ChatGPT Keeps Interrupting You — Dr. Tom Shapland, LiveKit
talk_summary: Tom Shapland explains why voice AI agents interrupt users: production turn-taking relies on a naive VAD (speech/not-speech plus a fixed silence threshold) rather than predicting end-of-turn from semantics, syntax, and prosody as humans do. He surveys augmentations (semantic end-of-utterance models over recent turns, audio-token smart-turn models, streaming STT that emits end-of-speech probability) and full-duplex models, concluding that cascade pipelines with smarter turn detection will win for production control.

takeaways.technique: Semantic end-of-turn prediction instead of fixed timeout
takeaways.what_they_do: A small transformer takes the last four turns (agent, user, agent, current user) and predicts an end-of-utterance token; if it says the turn isn't over, the fixed silence timer is extended rather than firing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the end of utterance token is saying that the end of turn it hasn't happened yet then we don't ... trigger the end of turn wait longer

takeaways.technique: Cheap small model as a gate in front of the expensive path
takeaways.what_they_do: A small open-weight model is inserted as one extra line in the pipeline to make a narrow binary decision (turn ended or not), leaving the main LLM untouched.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's just one more line in our in the pipeline that you you build ... It's open weight. It's you don't have to pay for it.

takeaways.technique: Give the judge the full conversation, not half the context
takeaways.what_they_do: He notes STT built-in end-of-utterance models only see the user's speech, not the agent's, so they lack full context — yet still work well; the LiveKit model deliberately includes both sides of the last four turns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're using your speechto texts builtin end of utterance model, it's only seeing half the context. It's only seeing what the user is saying.

takeaways.technique: Acknowledge no good benchmark; build a labeled set before tuning
takeaways.what_they_do: They admit their own benchmark numbers 'look great' but the industry lacks a good turn-taking benchmark, and they spent a call just figuring out how to get a good dataset.

takeaways.technique: Bounded recent-turn window for state decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: The semantic model uses exactly the last four turns as input — a fixed, small window — rather than the whole conversation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're taking the last four turns of the conversation as input
